elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: One stdlib probe driver owns subprocess timeout, byte caps, redaction and normalization for both adapters; provider-specific parsers are small additive functions returning the same closed record shape. The driver snapshots project `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` before and after each subprocess, excludes only its six declared Files from comparison, exits non-zero on any other delta and reports `project_delta=[]` on success. Do not pass `--dangerously-bypass-*`, expose environment, forward subagent text, persist sessions or let the probe write the project. Validate output schema independently after the provider returns. If a binary/auth/feature is absent, write `unknown|unsupported` with exact evidence and continue the other provider; do not mock a green runtime result.

elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: State derives only from strict replay; selection is deterministic over frozen IDs/dependencies; every activity has durable intent first and stable idempotency key; success envelope is only an observation; acceptance requires all frozen deterministic gates. At `READY`, a P2.3 decision with `allowed=false` and reason `RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` appends exactly the existing `budget_exhausted` event to `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, with the triggering slice/attempt/idempotency identity and exact closed decision as minimized evidence; it appends no intent and calls no activity. That run state is the v1 global admission breaker until explicit owner continue/abort. A cap observed after a boundary follows the legal observation/non-acceptance/reconcile path and trips `budget_exhausted` only after replay legally returns to `READY`. Default activity port refuses `provider_unavailable` before dispatch. Unknown/third state/source drift/failed rollback remains OWNER/incident and is never relabelled as budget exhaustion. RAG:— (repo-grounded: D3/D8–D13/D22/D35/D70 and the frozen transition/authority case banks).

elements.name: Code Guidance

For D70, assert the exact frozen authority decision and exact frozen state cell separately; a green final state alone is insufficient. No `while True`, implicit retry, plan-file write, provider name/argv, derived-only breaker flag or invented `circuit_breaker`/`repeated_finding` event is allowed. elements.value: Build rows only from the exact P1.6 smoke task/grant set and strict replay, never from P3.4's Task Contract/spec. Each manifest/admission pins one provider and unique run/slice/attempt/idempotency identity, task/grant/replay/source hashes and replay-derived usage; the index maps only the two frozen task IDs to exact files/hashes. `dispatch` loads READY state, recomputes every pin/counter, projects one scheduler slice and invokes the existing activity port. The default activity returns `provider_unavailable` after intent and never imports/spawns a provider; `start`/`resume` remain unchanged. RAG:— (repo-grounded: D74/D77 and P1.6 owners).

Independently mutate both provider rows, every identity/hash/usage/owner field and index mapping; prove cross-provider admission reuse refuses. Never default authority/budget fields, parse provider prose, catch broad exceptions, import P3 providers or accept merely well-formed/unsigned grants. If P1.6 cannot project a field, escalate against D77 rather than using P3.4 data.

elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: Finish and test the adapter native-tool projection plus write-heavy runner/activity binding before any live call. P2.6 verifies the exact indexed child-task admission, referenced grant, source pins and strict replay, then writes intent before activity; P3.4 receives only the projected worker request, typed task identity and exact admission-derived native-tool tuple. Provider/task/admission must match one-to-one. Claude empty tools become literal `--tools ""` with no `--allowedTools`; Codex empty tools and every unproven non-empty mapping return `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` before process. Installed CLI version drift returns `MAPPING_UNKNOWN` before process and never repins terminal probe/parity evidence. P3.4's Task Contract/item manifest, either grant, the admission index itself, cross-provider admission reuse and all P5 carriers refuse before intent/process. The runner never constructs authority/budget/usage, accepts, validates or retries. Each runnable attempt gets a new process/transient carrier; no session reuse/native children. Hard caps and minimized output are mandatory; timeout/overflow/kill uncertainty is closed failure/orphan. Only `dispatch` accepts explicit provider selection and one slice. Each smoke uses its admitted empty temporary Git repo with no reads/writes/tools and exact pre/post hash equality. Preserve P2's manifest/validator bytes; the P3 manifest pins their exact hash and `6c2c2ef3`, validates P2 rows against Git blobs at that commit, and independently pins current P3 files/evidence. Never run the P2 validator against the evolved root and report its expected hash failure as green. RAG:— (repo-grounded: D74/D77/D80/D81 and frozen admission/scheduler owners); RAG:✅ 2026-08-04 current provider controls/version drift in the new finding.

elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Keep provider semantics in `providers/{codex,claude_code}.py`; the activity/runner must not delete, inject or post-process argv flags. Make native tools a required immutable adapter input with no ambient/default fallback. For Claude, independently test empty and forbidden/unproven mappings, assert literal `--tools`, empty-string value and absence of `--allowedTools`/`Read,Glob,Grep`; for Codex, assert empty/unproven mappings raise the closed capability refusal before binary resolution/Popen, and never treat `read-only` as no-tool. If a later business tool mapping is needed, stop and require its owner-bound contract/probe rather than generalize during P3.4. Use `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` with selector/thread-safe bounded pipe draining; never `shell=True`, unbounded `communicate()`, `preexec_fn`, broad exception swallowing or PID-only kill. Keep time/kill/clock injectable and assert TERM→KILL plus verified group death. Attempt files use O_EXCL/0600 and are removed after normalized observation; a crash-left carrier is sensitive state, not reusable. The provider registry selects an adapter only after P2.6 returns an admitted request; no local default, grant parser or budget merge is legal. A capability/version/binary/auth/quota refusal produces an exact non-green readiness row with process count zero; it is not silently relaxed and does not claim provider maturity. Make `adapter-manifest-v1.json` the additive current-generation manifest with `base_prototype.path/sha256/git_commit` plus a closed current-file list; `validate-adapters.py` recomputes historical blobs with literal list argv `git show`, current hashes from disk and all referenced evidence. It must reject missing/shallow anchor, path traversal, duplicate/extra rows, baseline mutation, current drift, raw-content keys or fake-only live claims; never shell out through a command string.

elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: Before mutation, prove the exact P3.5 heading and `Files` exist in committed `HEAD` and the target plan carriers are clean; otherwise stop with `SPEC_NOT_COMMITTED`. Build the activity only after `dispatch.load_indexed_admission` and provider equality succeed. Adapter choice is exact registry data, never an `if unknown then default`. Preflight refusals (`CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, `MAPPING_UNKNOWN`, unavailable binary/version) return a closed normalized observation with `process_count=0` and never call the runner. A green mapping calls `worker.run` once with admission caps; its bounded bytes are folded inside an injected normalizer and discarded before the activity returns. The scheduler receives only the frozen neutral observation. Missing prompt/schema/MCP content whose bytes do not match the admitted hashes is `MAPPING_UNKNOWN`, not invented input. elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: Strict replay remains the sole authority and every fix lands in its owning existing module, including admission/replay verification fixes in `dispatch.py`. Reconcile observes a boundary before deciding: stale or grant-shaped admission refuses before intent; exact approved postimage is freshly validated then accepted; exact preimage records no-effect and may retry within budget; recognized partial rolls back the whole slice and verifies preimage; third state, missing backup, admission/source/replay drift or unverified orphan becomes incident/OWNER with zero further mutation. External counters prove one call per idempotency key. RAG:— (repo-grounded: D10–D11/D22/D43/D76 and terminal run/admission contracts).

elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Use P4.1's immutable rows and run each cut from a fresh process/root. Apply anti-self-deception: assert journal tail, external call counter, exact filesystem/process postimage and next legal command—not only returned status. Include both accepted and refusal paths, duplicate deliveries across two processes, crash after the public call before observation, crash after observation before acceptance, rollback failure and verified/unverified process death. Never add a blanket retry, “last line wins”, snapshot repair or fixture-specific exception. A missing contract transition is a D# escalation.

elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Apply the conformance anti-fitting pattern: write independent closed JSON cases and never derive expected actions, task eligibility or baseline selection from candidate output/enums. Read archives as bytes/JSON/Markdown data without adding them to `PYTHONPATH`; use exact allowlisted paths and deterministic sorted hashes/diagnostics. Include changed/missing archive, stale mapping, duplicate trial, post-first-event timestamp, baseline_pending/synthetic/unmatched lane, owner-event unmappable and accepted positive cases. A mapping gap or lack of five eligible waves blocks P5.2 rather than shrinking the catalog. **For the D121/D122 reopen:** treat v1 as read-only input, not as a template to edit in place — copy rows into a new object graph and diff the result against v1 to prove nothing leaked back. Prove the v2 set by independent recomputation, not by the generator's own exit code: recompute `catalog_hash`, every `task_hash`, `grant_hash`, `replay_hash` and `admission_hash` outside the writer and compare. Author the negative cases before the positive ones — wrong owner marker, D105 marker substituted for D122, missing D122 literal in `plan.md`, `reusable:true`, `max_slices:2`, a fourth row, a v1 trial ID reused, a changed file scope, a changed base commit, a second changed budget key, and a v2 admission presented where a v1 admission is expected (and the reverse) — and require each to refuse before write. Never generate an expected hash from the produced artifact. For rule (6), write the failing case first: a package that equals G2B but not G2 must PASS, a package that equals neither must FAIL, and a frozen admission whose `g2_package_digest` no longer equals the G2 predecessor must FAIL — three distinct cases, not one relaxed assertion. **For the D125/D127 reopen:** the pairing invariant is the whole point of the mint, so test it adversarially before the happy path — a baseline row whose `files` differ from its twin by one path, whose `base_commit` differs, whose `route` or any single budget key differs, whose `pair_id` points at a nonexistent twin, or where two candidate rows claim the same baseline — each must refuse before write. Add the negative cases for the grant boundary too: D105 or D122 marker substituted for D125, missing D125 literal in `plan.md`, `reusable:true`, `max_slices:2`, an eleventh row, a `codex` row, a v1 trial ID reused, and a v3 admission presented where a v1/v2 admission is expected (and each reverse). Recompute `catalog_hash` and every `task_hash`/`grant_hash`/`replay_hash`/`admission_hash` outside the writer and compare; never generate an expected hash from the produced artifact.

elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Apply conformance anti-fitting, anti-self-deception and if-then escalation patterns. Author the business output schema independently from the provider-projection manifest and validate it with a negative self-test before either adapter sees it. Author independent positive/negative cases before further runtime code: all 14 exact admissions accepted by the new loader; original G2 still rejects them; P2 smoke still passes; one-field mutations cover schema/version/hash/owner/expiry/revocation/provider/root/item/files/caps/replay/reuse; fake-binary provider argv cases prove the same real schema path and forbid bypass, resume, user config, MCP, network, child agents, version drift and unbounded tools without starting a provider. Never relabel the two failed D108 attempts, copy the P5.1 generator into package runtime, trust manifest hashes without recomputation, infer permission from prompt text, weaken a refusal, or generate expected rows from the partial implementation. Keep stdlib-only, list argv with `shell=False`, minimized observations and deterministic sorted diagnostics. For the D119 reopen specifically: a re-freeze is a mechanical recomputation, so prove it by recomputation, not by the validator's exit code alone — recompute both hashes independently of the writer and compare, and treat "the validator now says OK" as necessary but not sufficient. Never widen the seam while adopting it (no new CLI surface, no behavior change to `dispatch-business`, no test relaxation to make a hash match), and never edit a frozen row to make a diff smaller. **For the D121 reopen specifically:** write the refusal cases before the happy path — absent catalog file, catalog whose recomputed hash differs from the admission pin, admission `task_id` with no matching row, two rows with the same `trial_id`, and one case per cross-checked field (`files`, `base_commit`, `provider`, `route`, `capabilities`, `acceptance_refs`, `validation`, each `budgets` key) diverging by exactly one value — and assert each returns the named refusal with `process_count: 0` rather than a degraded prompt. Assert the composed prompt text directly in a test: it must contain the row's `scenario`, must name exactly the admission's `files` and no wider path, and must not contain `historical_patch_sha256`, any patch body or any current-tree source line. Prove the second re-freeze by independent recomputation of `generation_hash`/`assurance_hash` outside the writer, as D119 required — "the validator now says OK" is necessary, not sufficient. Do not add a CLI surface, do not change `dispatch-business` behavior, and do not relax an existing test to make a hash match. **For the D123/D127 reopen specifically:** build the fixtures from real provider record SHAPES (the key sets already asserted by `_RESULT_KEYS`/`ALLOWED_EVENTS`), never from a captured live payload, and write the negative cases first — a usage object missing `input_tokens`, a `total_cost_usd` absent, a `num_turns` absent, a codex record with no `usage` at all, and a record whose token value is a float or a string — each must produce `null` plus a named `unknown_reasons` entry, never a `0` and never a crash. Assert directly that `reasoning_tokens` is `0` WITH `inclusion_basis` for claude-code and an integer WITHOUT it for codex, and that no other field ever carries an `inclusion_basis`. Assert the coordinator envelope is seven zeros with a `zero_basis` that resolves to an existing committed path, and add a test that fails if that path stops existing. Prove the cost conversion on exact boundary values (`0`, `0.0000005`, `1.9999995`, a value with more than six decimals) with `Decimal`, and assert no `float` appears anywhere in the emitted object. Prove the third re-freeze by independent recomputation outside the writer, as both earlier reopens required — "the validator now says OK" is necessary, not sufficient. Never let a fold that refused emit an economy object, and never make an existing assertion weaker to accommodate the new key. **For the D132 reopen specifically:** write the failing case FIRST and prove it red on the pre-change module — a v3 admission refuses `ADMISSION_NOT_INDEXED` today, and after step one of two it refuses `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; a test that is green before the fix protects nothing, and this item's whole class exists because half a fix looked complete last time. Author these negative cases and require each to refuse: a batch key absent from the table; a v3 admission whose `owner_marker` is D105's; a v3 admission whose `branch` is `p5-business-trials`; a v1 admission whose `branch` is `p5-paired-battle-waves` (the swap the shared literal could not see); an index whose row count differs from the row's `expected_count`; a v3 admission presented against the v1 index path. Do not parameterize the tests over `GRANT_BATCHES` itself — a test that reads the same table it is checking passes on an empty table; name the three batch keys literally. Prove the seam-admission smoke by re-reading `used_slices` from disk before and after, not by trusting the command's own JSON. Never widen a check to make a row pass, never reorder refusals to make a test simpler, and never edit a v3 carrier byte to fit the package.

Under D119 the D118 package-owned seam is already part of the re-frozen G2B generation and is CONSUMED here, never edited: this item writes no `packages/artifex/**` byte and refreshes no manifest. If the seam turns out to need a change, that is an escalation to reopen P5.5 again — not an in-pilot patch. `run-pilot.py` stays a thin stateless caller of that package seam and must not reimplement argv construction, provider execution or result folding itself. Then execute exactly the three P5.2 admissions in catalog order through the bridge after `dispatch-business` admission, with explicit controlled root and one-slice caps; refuse P3 reuse, local mint/reset, provider reduction or G2 fallback. **D121/D122 re-run rules (these govern the live work; the rules above continue to apply unchanged except where an identity or path is named).** (1) Two upstream preconditions are hard gates, checked before any mutation: reopened P5.1 is terminal and its v2 validator run exits 0 over `trial-admission-index-v2-p5.2-retry.json`, and twice-reopened P5.5 is terminal with `validate-business-successor.py` exiting 0 and its re-frozen `g2b_generation_hash` equal to the digest recomputed live over current `packages/artifex` bytes. elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Keep `run-pilot.py` stdlib-only and stateless apart from bounded local invocation results; list argv, explicit roots, `shell=False`, caps/timeouts and no ambient discovery. Apply anti-self-deception: assert strict journal tail, worker/process freshness, attempt/call IDs, full Git delta, acceptance commands, terminal packet and pre/post/rollback hashes—not only exit 0. Include dry-run/fake fixtures for early OWNER, third state, path drift, fourth-slice attempt, raw-content field and P4 hash drift. Never patch candidate/P4 evidence to make the pilot pass. Two additional hard bans from D119/D120: never edit a `packages/artifex/**` byte or a G2B manifest to make a gate pass — a seam defect is an escalation that reopens P5.5, not an in-pilot fix; and never silently fall back to the PATH `claude` binary when the pinned build is missing — refuse before intent and say so. **For the D121/D122 re-run:** before interpreting any observation, inspect the disposable worktree at the frozen base and record, per slice, which declared files exist there and which do not — the first pilot's closing finding drew its causal conclusion from the current tree instead, and got it exactly backwards (`findings/P5.2-task-description-gap-2026-08-06.md` F4). Record the resolved `scenario` string the seam actually used, per slice, in the results file, so the next reader can tell a stated task from a missing one without re-deriving it. Treat a zero-diff `success` as a first-class outcome to be reported, never as an acceptance and never as a reason to re-dispatch. Keep `run-pilot.py` a thin caller: v2 paths arrive as explicit arguments, no constant is hardcoded that also lives in a manifest, and nothing about prompt composition exists in this file. If the re-run again yields 0/3, do not retry, do not adjust the validator, and do not edit the seam — report the honest result with the per-slice base-tree inventory and the resolved scenarios, and let the plan decide.

elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: Author `validate-economic-verdict.py` and its cases BEFORE the first dispatch; nothing about the adjudicator is written after seeing a result. Run the full pre-intent gate first and stop before intent if any part is red: P5.6's three repaired validators, `validate-contract-set.py` on the v2 manifest, `validate-economy-evidence.py` on the v2 set, `validate-trial-admissions.py` on all three carrier sets, `validate-business-successor.py`, `validate-repository-pilot.py` (**D130:** its green for this gate is exit `2` — evidence intact with P5.2's immutable honest `0/3 accepted` report; exit `1` is the only red, and exit `0` is unreachable because those three D122 admissions are one-shot and spent), `validate-recovery-pilot.py` in P5.8's repaired form (with `--ledger`), `validate-assurance.py` in P5.8's repaired form over P4.8's full twelve-argument list, `validate-provenance-reconciliation.py` in its THREE-argument form `--record … --plan-dir … --self-test` (the previous spec text named `--self-test` alone, which exits 2 on an argparse error before reaching the gate — a spec-text defect corrected here, not a relaxed check), the P4 evidence anchor in D134's TWO-command form (`git diff --exit-code 3533234c -- phases/P4.md artifacts/P4 ':(exclude)artifacts/P4/validate-assurance.py'` empty AND `git log --format=%h 3533234c..HEAD -- artifacts/P4/validate-assurance.py` returning exactly P5.8's item commit), and `bash packages/artifex/scripts/test.sh`. One additional pre-intent check precedes the first dispatch and costs nothing: a validate-only `dispatch-business` of ONE v3 row must return `"status":"admitted"` with `"intent_written":false` and leave `used_slices` at `0` — the seam-admission smoke of `research/41-…` §3; a refusal here stops before intent and belongs to P5.5, not to this item. Then perform the single D109 generation-aware P0–P5 fan-in: historical leaves at their owning commits, current G2B successor/package/provider/contract/assurance on the current tree, no stale-status replay. Before each of the ten dispatches, re-probe the pinned `claude-code` binary through `SKM_CLAUDE_BIN` and refuse before intent if it prints anything but `2.1.222 (Claude Code)` (D120); recompute the exact G2B package/CLI identity, verify it equals the ledger's last entry, and validate its immutable G2 predecessor; then select the exact unused D125 admission and recompute its owner/catalog/request/G2-predecessor/G2B/provider/root/task/caps/replay/expiry pins. D105 and D122 carriers, P3 smoke carriers, P5.5 probes, historical G1 substitution, local mint or refresh, admission reuse, row substitution and any `codex` invocation all refuse before intent. Execute the pair members on adjacent disposable roots in frozen catalog order, one fresh process each, no retry of a started attempt, rolling every root back to its exact base and removing it — and inspect each root's `git diff` BEFORE removal, because a removed worktree cannot be re-read (the P5.2 evidence gap this rule exists to prevent). The baseline member runs through the same runner and the same measurement extraction, but WITHOUT the supervisor: one direct headless invocation under the same budget envelope, and its `coordinator` envelope is the same structural zero with the same `zero_basis` as the candidate's. Recompute every economy, intervention and retry total from per-attempt rows under `economy-evidence-v2` — never trust a summary total, never scrape prose, never fetch or apply a price, never treat an absent event as zero, and never rerun only the failing side of a pair. Reliability and security floors are evaluated before economics. Terminal success requires every D14/D25/D49 floor GREEN, at least one eligible branch and the literal `GO`; the verdict is emitted in `single-provider` mode with `owner_grant_ref` naming D123 and is never rendered as parity (D126). G3 records the exact G2B generation/assurance/package digest measured and proves no post-P5.5 package delta. Missing, expired, revoked, synthetic, unknown, ineligible or unmatched evidence retains `NO-GO`, emits the exact failed floors, appends no terminal Completion Notes and returns to plan-design for bounded forward items before a fresh full adjudication. RAG:— (owner/repo-grounded: D14/D18/D25/D49/D53–D54/D78/D85/D108–D109/D120/D123–D127 and the frozen contracts).

elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: (1) The invariant every repair must express is TWO-SIDED, exactly as D121/D122 rule (6) states it: a FROZEN carrier is proven against the snapshot it was cut at, and the LIVE tree is compared against the CURRENT G2B generation resolved at run time from `business-successor-generation-v1.json`. Never hard-code a generation or commit literal into a validator — P5.5's third re-freeze will move the generation again, and the anchors are all resolvable from Git (`git log -1 --format=%H -- <path>`); a literal would re-break every gate this item just fixed. (2) Do not delete a check, do not make it optional behind a flag, and do not widen it to "any digest": each repaired check must still fail on a package that equals neither generation and on a frozen carrier whose predecessor pin drifted. (3) D128 — the `business carriers exist before exact owner grant` guard is MOVED, never dropped. In `validate()` it becomes the historical form: resolve the shadow-freeze commit at run time (the single commit shared by `trial-catalog-v1.json`/`archive-mapping-v1.json`/`shadow-results-v1.json`/`business-grant-request-v1.json`; if those four ever disagree on their newest commit, STOP and escalate rather than pick one), then prove through `git ls-tree` on THAT commit that none of the six named business carriers and no `trial-admissions/` tree existed. In `main()` the live form is a refusal raised BEFORE the `--write` branch writes its first byte — today the check runs after the write, which is itself part of the defect. (4) D129 — for repair (2) the frozen anchor is resolved at run time as the newest commit that changed `package-promotion-manifest-v1.json`; `--historical-commit` stays as an explicit override for the historical replays that already pass it. Passing that flag ALONE is not the repair: the existing branch skips the current-tree comparison entirely, so the live half (current package equals the sole G2B digest) must be added, and the corrected `--prototype` literal is `artifacts/P3/adapter-manifest-v1.json`, matching P3.md's own line for the same script. (5) The ledger is a RECORD, not an authority: build `g2b-generation-ledger-v1.json` by reading git history of `business-successor-generation-v1.json`, one entry per commit that actually CHANGED `generation_hash` (re-derive each hash from `git show <commit>:<path>`, never from a table in prose), each carrying the hash, the commit, the date and the one-line reason taken from that commit's own item record; never invent an entry, never reorder, never remove, and require the last entry to equal the live value. The acceptance count and the honest report line stay in the output verbatim. elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Write the failing case FIRST for each repair, and prove it goes red on the pre-repair validator — a test that is already green before the fix protects nothing. Per repaired validator author three distinct cases, never one relaxed assertion: a package equal to the current G2B passes; a package equal to neither G2 nor G2B fails; a frozen carrier whose `g2_package_digest` no longer equals the immutable G2 predecessor fails. For D128 add two: a synthetic history in which a business carrier already existed at the freeze commit must FAIL the historical assertion, and `--write` invoked while a business carrier exists must refuse WITHOUT having written a single byte (assert the four target files' mtimes/bytes are untouched after the refusal). For the ledger add two: a recorded pilot hash absent from the ledger fails, and a ledger whose last entry differs from the live generation fails. For D130 add three, one per code: intact evidence with every slice accepted → `0`; intact evidence with the recorded `0/3` → `2` with the honest report printed; a stale/mutated input → `1`. Keep every validator stdlib-only, deterministic and sorted in its diagnostics, and make each diagnostic name BOTH sides of the comparison (which digest was expected, which was found, and which generation each belongs to) — the F4 diagnostic was readable precisely because it printed both, and that is the standard to hold. Do not refactor a validator beyond the repaired check, do not unify the three scripts into a shared module in this item, and never make an assertion weaker to reach exit 0. If a repair requires reading git history, shell out to `git` with an explicit path list and parse deterministically; never infer history from file mtimes or from the plan's prose. The (1a) draft already in the working tree is verified correct — adopt it, do not rewrite it, and do not revert it to "start clean". If any repair looks like it needs a recorded byte to move, or the four frozen carriers disagree on their freeze commit, STOP and escalate (§10) — a second stop costs one session, a quietly weakened gate costs the plan its evidence.

elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Author the adversarial cases before the contract text is final and let them drive it — a rule that cannot be expressed as a failing case is not a rule. Required negative cases, each of which must be REJECTED: a bare `0` where the field is simply unreported (no `inclusion_basis`); an `inclusion_basis` on any field other than the one closed instantiation row; an `inclusion_basis` naming a field that is itself null; a `zero_basis` pointing at a path that does not exist in the tree; a `zero_basis` on an envelope whose component demonstrably can call a model; a `cost_microunits` derived from tokens times a rate; a float or a rounded percentage anywhere; `single-provider` mode with an empty owner D# reference; and a `single-provider` result rendered as parity. Required positive cases: every existing v1 case re-run unchanged under v2 with the same outcome (a v2 that changes a v1 verdict is a regression, not an upgrade — assert this explicitly), plus one full claude-code candidate/baseline pair that passes with the two sanctioned bases present. Never derive an expected verdict from an implementation's output; compute the D14 arithmetic independently with integers and rational cross-multiplication, exactly as v1 requires. elements.name: Implementation Rules
elements.value: Run from a cold session whose actor/session differs from P6.2/P6.3 and record that provenance. Recompute every generation manifest/hash and expected product surface from raw minimized evidence; do not trust summary verdicts or compare an evolved current tree to a historical generation. GREEN requires literal frozen P5 `GO` over G2B, exact G2→G2B predecessor and D108 scope/probe/zero-D105-usage evidence, exact non-revoked D86/D87/D95/D96, valid D93/D97 mappings, valid G1→G2→G2B→G3→G4→G5 pins, one package runtime owner, protected runtime identity, working standalone and umbrella lifecycle, generated parity, compatibility, rollback, privacy and green validation. Any red/skipped/degraded required check emits RED plus a scoped remediation target and keeps P6/the plan non-terminal; the auditor does not fix it. RAG:— (owner/repo-grounded: D60–D61/D85–D109 and evidence-integrity canon).

elements.name: Code Guidance
elements.value: Author the independent audit validator against closed cases and raw manifests, not by importing P6.1–P6.3 validators as verdict functions. Include forged summary, altered scope, independently missing D86/D87/D95/D96, use of superseded D91/D92 as active grants, extra Harness path, wrong `--authorize` order, lock-as-authorize-target, duplicate plan/package import, missing standalone or umbrella CLI, broken install/doctor, implicit enable, backup/hash mismatch, stale generated files, docs only umbrella/not standalone, leaked forbidden key, foreign diff and a complete positive branch. Reject-all must fail positive controls. Keep the audit read-only outside its own plan artifacts.

elements.name: Validation
elements.value: All terminal P0–P6.3 validators rerun green in declared current/historical modes; `validate-release-candidate-audit.py` additionally consumes P5.5 generation/assurance and independently proves one complete GREEN G1→G2→G2B→G3→G4→G5 product branch, all exact owner carriers and both D93 generation/lock transitions with positive controls. Altered/missing D108, provider-version/probe/usage or predecessor pins, current-vs-historical substitution, protected-runtime drift, unauthorized Harness path, stale root projection or one-provider-only guide fails. Harness/package/skiller/bootstrap/registry/docs/standalone/umbrella checks, forbidden-key scan and `git diff --check` are green.

elements.name: Deliverables
elements.value: Independent cold audit JSON/validator/human verdict over the complete generation/instruction/product chain and evidence needed for `task:plan-close ... P6`; RED names the owning item and preserves phase/plan non-terminal, GREEN permits successful plan closure but not tag/push/publish.

elements.name: Escalation Needed
elements.value: no

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Artifex v1 проектируется как внешний durable supervisor, а не named Workflow, agent-pack orchestrator или длинная parent-agent сессия. RAG:✅ current OpenAI/Anthropic long-horizon and subagent docs; repo-grounded current Harness inspection.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Workflow повторно раздувает coordinator context и не владеет durable execution state; живой `_common.orchestrator` только планирует для main session.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: До P5 кандидат живёт plan-local под `plans/2026.08.03-ARTIFEX-SUPERVISOR/artifacts/supervisor/`; `packages/artifex/` и root CLI не создаются. RAG:— (repo-grounded: five-package, CLI-routing and speculative-work canons).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Проверяем проблему до расширения архитектуры и не создаём шестой package по ожиданию.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Supervisor scheduler/arbiter/recovery path детерминирован; LLM calls являются activities за side-effect boundary и не принимают state-transition решения. RAG:✅ Temporal workflow/activity patterns; adapted without dependency.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Replay должен давать тот же переход без повторного модельного суждения.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Authority precedence: system/security/provider hard limits → root/package instructions → frozen plan contracts/D# → signed run mandate, который может только сужать → supervisor defaults. RAG:— (internal authority policy).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Нижний слой не может отменить верхний; конфликт становится машинно разрешимым либо OWNER.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Действия делятся на `AUTO`, `AUTO-FIX`, `OWNER`; класс вычисляется из scope, reversibility, external visibility, contract/public-API/dependency/security и validation predicates, а не из рекомендации worker. RAG:— (internal policy synthesized from repository authority canons).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Рекомендация модели не является разрешением.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: При нескольких legal AUTO-вариантах supervisor выбирает минимальный blast radius, простейший reversible вариант и пишет decision reason; canon conflict или недоказанная эквивалентность переходят в OWNER. RAG:— (owner brief).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Так автоматизируется рутинное согласие владельца без угадывания новых канонов.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Каждый слайс получает fresh worker, immutable minimal context bundle и capped structured return; полный parent transcript не переносится. RAG:✅ OpenAI/Anthropic subagent docs.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Изоляция шума экономит coordinator context; сами subagents не объявляются бесплатными по токенам.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Дефолт — последовательный one-writer scheduler. Parallel max 2 разрешён только по доказанной независимости: read-only fan-out либо отдельные worktrees; merge/integration всегда сериализован. RAG:✅ OpenAI caution for write-heavy parallel work; Maestro/Superset worktree patterns.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Предотвращает конфликтный fan-out и стоимость повторной интеграции.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Prototype state — hash-chained append-only JSONL + derived atomic snapshot + exclusive writer lock; SQLite/Temporal не являются runtime dependencies. RAG:✅ SQLite WAL and Temporal recovery principles; adapted to stdlib.

elements.name: why
elements.value: JSONL прозрачен, переносим и не зависит от host SQLite WAL/version semantics.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Каждая side-effect boundary использует `intent → fsync/reopen/verify → call → observation → fsync/reopen/verify → acceptance`; intent несёт stable run/slice/attempt/idempotency key и source/input hashes. RAG:— (reliability design adapted from durable execution patterns and current P5/P6 WAL precedent).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Crash не должен превращать неизвестный side effect в молчаливый повтор.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Resume/reconcile принимает только exact approved postimage, exact preimage либо контрактно распознанный partial с whole-slice rollback; third state, torn/reordered chain, source drift или missing backup отказывают. RAG:— (repo-grounded P6 WAL precedent; external durable-execution synthesis).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Восстановление не угадывает состояние.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Codex и Claude являются additive provider adapters одного `worker-envelope-v1`; approvals, exits, quota, budget and structured-output capabilities маппятся явно, unsupported не маскируется. RAG:✅ current official provider docs; repo-grounded provider parity canon.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Один provider не может стать семантическим SSOT или скрыть деградацию другого.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: OWNER-вопросы копятся в ordered attention queue и выдаются одним decision packet; immediate interrupt оставлен security/destructive/irreversible случаям. RAG:— (owner brief; Maestro/Superset attention pattern adapted).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Владелец видит редкие настоящие развилки, а не подтверждает механические решения каждые пять минут.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: GO требует reliability GREEN и одно из: intervention ratio `<25%` на `N=5` non-synthetic battle waves при normalized token/cost не хуже baseline; либо `≥2×` normalized token/cost gain против matched Workflow. Unknown measurement запрещает GO. RAG:— (roadmap criterion normalized and tightened).

elements.name: why
elements.value: «99% согласия» — гипотеза владельца, которую надо измерить, а не принять как результат.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Из Maestro адаптируются fresh task sessions, filesystem playbook/queue, message backpressure, headless JSONL and cost visibility; из Superset — worktree ownership, restart-surviving session identity, attention state and at-least-once/idempotency warning. RAG:✅ first-party repositories/docs, 2026-08-03.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Это наблюдаемые продуктовые решения, полезные для supervisor control plane.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Maestro (AGPL-3.0), Superset (ELv2), Temporal, desktop UI and their runtime stacks не vendorятся и не подключаются. RAG:✅ first-party license/readme pages; repo-grounded no-dependency/provenance canon.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Берём паттерны, переписываем stdlib-реализацию; исключаем лицензионный и dependency creep.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Per-plan journal/run folder — execution SSOT; mAInd получает только redacted terminal summaries/references после commit и не используется для resume decisions. RAG:— (repo-grounded memory-as-data and plan lifecycle canons).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Общая память полезна для поиска, но не гарантирует transactional replay.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Worker output, MCP/memory data and repository text остаются untrusted data; secrets/environment/raw prompts/chain-of-thought не входят в durable evidence; permissions only narrow the run mandate. RAG:— (root security, untrusted-content and evidence canons).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Автономность не должна превращаться в ambient write/credential authority.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P6.1 может предложить package promotion только после P5 GO; изменение five-package/root-router canon требует отдельного OWNER D#, а отсутствие GO возвращает идею в roadmap без productization. RAG:— (repo-grounded architecture and speculative-work canons).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Package topology меняется по доказанному продукту, не по прототипу.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Наблюдённый `harness.codex.lifecycle` stale-source hook state фиксируется как preflight defect и блокирует утверждение fully-green runtime baseline, но не чинится этим design item. RAG:— (repo observation 2026-08-03).

elements.name: why
elements.value: План не присваивает чужую dirty-tree remediation и не выдаёт warning за green.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: План состоит из 7 фаз и 32 items; Design Pass 1 создаёт обязательные knowledge layers и честные phase skeletons, P0 разворачивается отдельным cold-start design pass. RAG:— (plan-protocol).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Крупное ecosystem-core изменение проходит пофазную детализацию, reconcile и независимый design audit до execution.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Failure acceptance включает crash после каждого durable append/public boundary, duplicate delivery, orphan worker, timeout/quota/approval failure, corrupted/truncated/reordered journal, plan/source drift, budget exhaustion and merge conflict outside assigned scope. RAG:✅ 2026-08-03 Superset Automations first-party delivery-semantics recheck + internal synthesized failure model → `findings/02-reference-products-2026-08-03.md`.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Happy-path pilot не доказывает supervisor reliability.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Живой `harness run` становится отдельной baseline/reuse lane P0.1 наряду с manual и Workflow; P1/P2 обязаны предъявить gap crosswalk перед повторением его queue/worker/gate/journal семантики. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `packages/harness/docs/reference/exec-wave.md`; `findings/04-p0-design-verification-2026-08-03.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Bootstrap верно отрицал durable supervisor, но пропустил уже существующий последовательный exec-wave driver; игнорировать его означало бы проектировать дубликат.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P0 freeze хранится тройкой «читаемый Markdown + нормализованный JSON + stdlib verifier»; raw provider streams, prompts, chain-of-thought, secrets и environment dumps в evidence bundle не входят. RAG:— (repo-grounded: evidence-integrity/untrusted-content canons and `research/06-p0-evidence-freeze-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Человек должен видеть основания, а следующий дешёвый исполнитель — проверять форму без доверия к прозе или сырым модельным данным.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Отсутствующая историческая метрика закрывает P0.1 как честный `baseline_pending` с `unknown_reason`, но блокирует любой P5 economic GO branch, которому она нужна; ноль не импутируется. RAG:— (owner-grounded acceptance intent; `research/04-token-economy-and-acceptance.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: P0 фиксирует качество доступного evidence, а не фабрикует цифры; экономический вердикт остаётся fail-closed.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P0 исполняется последовательно без Workflow: P0.2 зависит от baseline/reuse границ P0.1, P0.4 — от authority/provider evidence, P0.5 — от P0.1–P0.4; все items имеют `Exec = manual`. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/06-p0-evidence-freeze-design.md`; plan-protocol orchestration criterion).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Фаза не имеет трёх независимых plan-exec slices и не является автономной внешней цепочкой; orchestration carrier здесь создаст лишний контекст и второй scheduler.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Design budget registrar исправлен с 3 до 8 проходов: bootstrap + отдельные cold-start P0–P6, затем `finish`; это уточняет D21 без изменения семи фаз. **Consequences:** до исполнения добавляются пять обязательных design-сессий P2–P6. RAG:— (repo-grounded: plan-protocol phase-by-phase pipeline; seven-phase board).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Старый знаменатель достигался уже на P1 и противоречил обязательному handoff на оставшиеся скелеты; качество ecosystem-core плана важнее преждевременного `finish`.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P1 замораживает пять отдельных contracts в порядке run → slice → authority → worker → economy; каждый несёт Markdown + independent JSON cases + stdlib validator, а P1.5 — aggregate manifest/validator. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/07-p1-contract-freeze-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Mega-contract стирает ownership/versioning; один общий validator даёт поздним items возможность переинтерпретировать ранние expected outcomes.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P1 execution hard-gated на terminal P0 и green P0 validators; пока P0 0/5, его outputs именуются только как planned preconditions. Donor contracts цитируются, а не копируются; P1 добавляет только supervisor-owned seams. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/05-p1-donor-reconciliation-2026-08-03.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Design может быть DoR до producer execution, но frozen values нельзя изобретать из будущих files или дублировать live Task/Harness carriers.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P1 не создаёт workflow: P1.2 потребляет P1.1, P1.3 — P1.2, P1.4 — P1.2/P1.3, P1.5 — P1.1–P1.4; все пять contract items manual frontier/high. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/07-p1-contract-freeze-design.md`; plan-protocol binary orchestration criterion).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Ни независимый N≥3 fan-out, ни длинная autonomous chain без manual contract checkpoints не существуют.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P1 high-stakes pre-mortem связывает invented P0 evidence, duplicate SSOT, authority widening, provider leakage, replay duplication, contract-set drift и metric/privacy gaming с наблюдаемыми сигналами, mitigations и owners P1.1–P1.5. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/07-p1-contract-freeze-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Ecosystem-core contract freeze не считается ready без владельца каждой причины отказа через 6–12 месяцев.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P2 compiler consumes the worktree-local `harness run --dry-run --json` queue plus canonical `task.task_contract build` output through subprocesses; it cross-checks them and adds only `slice-manifest-v1` semantics. It neither imports private parsers nor parses Markdown. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/06-p2-runtime-recon-2026-08-03.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Reuses the live reader/route owners without binding the experiment to their private Python seams or creating a third status/parser SSOT.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P2 run storage uses strict canonical hash-chain JSONL, a POSIX advisory single-writer lock and derived atomic snapshots; locking, name replacement and durability are separate evidence claims, and unsupported directory durability stays explicit. RAG:✅ Python 3.12 official API boundaries in `findings/06-p2-runtime-recon-2026-08-03.md`.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Tolerant analytics readers and non-fsync `core.io` writes cannot be reused for a recovery authority; product portability/physical durability remains P4/P6 evidence.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P2 has no production provider adapter: its default activity port refuses before dispatch, and only deterministic fakes may drive tests. Codex/Claude argv, event parsing and capability degradation belong exclusively to P3. RAG:— (repo-grounded: phase contracts and provider-parity canon).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Durable-core correctness must be testable without credentials or provider effects, and provider empirical seams must not leak backward into the neutral core.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P2 executes sequentially P2.1→P2.5 with no Workflow; each item is `implementation/high`, `Exec = manual`, full review. **Consequences:** the draft `P2.1–P2.5 implementation/high plan-exec` row is replaced by five legal rows and every P2 item needs a routed manual session. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/08-p2-prototype-design.md`; plan-protocol routing/orchestration rules).

elements.name: why
elements.value: All items form one producer chain; `plan-exec` cannot satisfy high effort, and a workflow would become a second scheduler before the candidate is proven.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P3 keeps Codex/Claude as separate pure argv/event mappers over `worker-envelope-v1`; one shared P3.4 process runner alone owns subprocess, timeout, caps, redaction and orphan handling. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/09-p3-provider-adapter-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Additive adapters preserve the P1 neutral SSOT, while one runner prevents the reliability boundary from drifting by provider.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Every attempt starts a new non-persistent provider process with no resume/continue/session reuse; native child-agent surfaces are disabled, and any non-disabled child policy is capability-unsupported/OWNER in v1. RAG:✅ current non-persistence/tool/feature controls in `findings/07-p3-provider-runtime-recon-2026-08-03.md`; child refusal is internal policy.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Current CLIs do not expose one proven common hard cap for child count, scope and budget; a prompt-only limit is not authority.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P3 permissions are explicit and narrowing-only: Codex uses the verified sandbox plus non-interactive approval config, Claude uses `dontAsk` plus exact available/allowed tools; bypass/yolo, ambient fallback and `--bare` are forbidden. RAG:✅ 2026-08-03 official permission/CLI facts in `findings/07-p3-provider-runtime-recon-2026-08-03.md`; mapping is contract-driven.

elements.name: why
elements.value: A headless worker must refuse rather than wait for approval, widen authority or discard repository instructions/hooks.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P3.4 binds adapters through P2's typed activity port and adds only explicit provider selection plus hard `--max-slices 1` to existing `start`/`resume`; omission preserves P2's no-provider refusal. RAG:— (repo-grounded: D34 and `research/09-p3-provider-adapter-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Provider integration stays additive, one scheduler/state machine remains authoritative, and the prototype cannot become an unattended wave before P4/P5 evidence.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P3 executes sequentially P3.1→P3.4 without Workflow; all four items are `implementation/high`, `Exec = manual`, full review. RAG:— (repo-grounded: P3 dependency graph and plan-protocol orchestration criterion).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Only two provider mappers are independently shaped; parity and the shared runner depend on both, so N≥3 independent items and long external autonomous chain are absent.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P3 preflight records two non-green Hook/Harness facts without repair: relative `--target .` raises explicit-root `ValueError`, while absolute target still reports lifecycle hooks/handler `stale-source`; syntax, doctor and mAInd health are green. RAG:— (direct local observation; `findings/07-p3-provider-runtime-recon-2026-08-03.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Validation trust must distinguish a CLI-normalization defect, actual source drift and unrelated green checks; this design pass does not capture foreign dirty scope.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P4 freezes an independent exact-set fault matrix and child-process cut-point harness before recovery fixes: every durable append/reopen and provider/Git/validation boundary gets before/after rows, plus positive reachability. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/10-p4-assurance-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Candidate-owned chaos selection or mock-only exceptions could omit the boundary that actually loses state and could let reject-all pass.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P4.2 repairs only existing P2/P3 store/scheduler/worker/CLI owners; unresolved intent is observed before action and may become exact-post accept, exact-pre retry-with-budget, recognized-partial whole-slice rollback or third-state OWNER—never blind rerun. RAG:— (repo-grounded: D10–D11, `research/10-p4-assurance-design.md`).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Preserves one state machine and makes duplicate external calls machine-observable through stable idempotency keys/counters.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: A write-capable attempt uses a detached identity-locked linked worktree at a pinned base; stable inventory comes from `git worktree list --porcelain -z`, and `--force`/broad prune are forbidden. RAG:✅ 2026-08-03 current official Git worktree semantics in `findings/08-p4-recovery-security-recon-2026-08-03.md`.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Git documents separate working/index state but shared repository state; exact ownership is required before cleanup or integration.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: Linked worktrees prove file/index write-lane isolation only, not security. D119 supersedes only the assumption — carried by D118's Consequences and P5.2's Scope Included — that P5.2 owns the D118 execution-seam bytes; D118's architecture verdict (package-owned, reusing existing business argv/fold/activity/worker primitives) is unchanged and remains the design. No new owner grant is created and none is needed: D108 stays the authority (`revoked=false`, `consumer=P5.5 only`), its finite `capability_probes=2` are untouched because the re-freeze launches no provider process (`validate-business-successor.py --write` accepts the two already-recorded R2 observations, which its read path already revalidates against the same closed wrapper contract), and D113's terminal-evidence acceptance rule carries those same rows over verbatim. Rejected: granting P5.2 the re-freeze right (would need a new grant superseding the phase `Границы` and D109, and would let the measuring item author the measured G2B digest that P5.3/P5.4/P6 pin — measurement self-certification); reverting the seam into `run-pilot.py` (contradicts D118 and P5.2's own Scope Excluded, already voided once as D116/D117). **Consequences:** P5.5's terminality must be re-earned instead of assumed; the G2B `generation_hash` moves off `7c1187f0a3f8addda07a27ea36cda836ffd64f91281cf56ac95a7fcb04da7a30` to the value recomputed at re-freeze (`f13c30f25dc50075669dd97f7ab4c8ec2fd9e54260e5359adbfe34c33ef0fcc6` for the current tree, valid only while no further package byte changes), so every downstream G2B pin in P5.2–P5.4/P6 refers to the re-frozen digest; P5 spends one extra producer cycle before the first pilot. Unchanged: D105 (14/14 rows unused, expiry `2026-08-12T23:59:59Z`, caps, roots), D111/D112 R2 controls, immutable G2/P4/P5.1 bytes, D117's void of D114–D116. elements.value: D109 already prescribed that successor drift reopens P5.5 rather than being patched inside a pilot; applying that rule keeps one producer for the executable boundary, needs no invented authority, and prevents the pilot from defining the very digest it measures.

elements.value: [OWNER-SELECTION:P5.2-VERSION-PIN] Shown that the PATH `claude` is `2.1.223 (Claude Code)` while the frozen pin is `2.1.222 (Claude Code)`, the owner literally selected «Гонять 2.1.222 (рекоменд.)» (`brief/33-p5.2-seam-ownership-owner-decision-2026-08-06.md`). The pin is HONORED, not bumped: the pilot resolves the Claude binary through the already-existing `SKM_CLAUDE_BIN` override (`packages/artifex/lib/artifex/providers/claude_code.py:27-32`, which reads it before `shutil.which("claude")`) pointed at `/home/vostrikov/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.222`, whose `--version` prints the exact frozen literal. No frozen text of `business-dispatch-admission-v1@1.0.0`, no `provider-business-projection-v1.json` row and no `providers/claude_code.BUSINESS_VERSION` constant changes; Codex `codex-cli 0.146.0` already matches its pin. This is therefore not the "provider-version drift" case D109 routes to a P5.5 reopen — there is no drift once the pinned build is the one executed — and it creates no owner grant. Rejected: bumping the pin to `2.1.223` (needs a new grant to edit a frozen contract, reopens P5.5 for a second reason, and would rest every provider claim on a CLI surface never verified first-party at that version). **Consequences:** P5.2's Implementation Rules gain a hard pre-dispatch obligation to re-probe the pinned binary's literal at execution time and refuse before intent if it is absent or prints anything else — the local version manager may prune old builds — and every P5.2–P5.4 pilot invocation must carry the same explicit binary pin rather than inheriting PATH. RAG:✅ 2026-08-06 first-party local probes (`claude --version` → `2.1.223 (Claude Code)`; `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.222 --version` → `2.1.222 (Claude Code)`; `codex --version` → `codex-cli 0.146.0`) captured in `findings/P5.2-seam-ownership-and-version-drift-2026-08-06.md` F3/F4; owner-grounded: `brief/33-p5.2-seam-ownership-owner-decision-2026-08-06.md`.

elements.name: why
elements.value: A frozen pin exists to make the measurement reproducible; honoring it with the build that is still on disk costs nothing and keeps the contract, the manifest and the runtime constant mutually consistent, while a bump would trade a solved problem for an unverified provider surface and a second reopen.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: [OWNER-SELECTION:P5.2-TASK-DESCRIPTION-CARRIER] The repository owner was shown the verified root cause of P5.2's `0/3 accepted` and four options, and literally selected «Реопен P5.5 + новый грант на 3 строки (реком.)» (`brief/34-p5.2-zero-accept-owner-decision-2026-08-06.md`). Verified cause, not inference: the frozen D105 admission's `task` object carries no natural-language task description at all (twenty fields, none of them a statement of what to do), the frozen P5.1 catalog does carry it (`scenario` = "reconstruct bounded subset of feat(artifex): изолировать worktree-интеграцию (P4.3)", plus `kind` and `historical_patch_sha256`), and `build-trial-admissions.py:158-181` silently drops all three when minting the admission — so `activity.BusinessProviderActivityPort._prompt`, whose only input is `task["files"]`, physically cannot state the task. At the frozen base `bde07fb0` slice-01's two and slice-03's three declared files do not exist in the tree, so codex was asked to "implement the bounded repository slice" in nonexistent paths with no statement of what to build; the closing P5.2 finding's contrary reading ("already complete, terminal, tested bytes") described the current working tree, not the disposable worktree the provider saw, and is corrected by `findings/P5.2-task-description-gap-2026-08-06.md` F4. **The fix is producer-side and hash-only:** P5.5 reopens `🟠 Done with deviations` → `🟡 In progress` and teaches the business activity port to load the catalog file whose `catalog_hash` equals the admission's already-pinned `task.catalog_hash`, select the row by `task_id`, and compose a prompt that states the scenario — no admission byte, no frozen-contract text and no D105 binding changes, and the port already resolves a frozen plan artifact by path at dispatch time (the output schema), so this is the same architectural move. P5.1 reopens `🟢 Done` → `🟡 In progress` as the plan's sole carrier producer to mint an ADDITIVE v2 carrier set for D122's three replacement rows (measurement self-certification stays banned: the measuring item never mints its own authority — same rule D119 applied to the G2B producer). P5.2 reopens `🟠 Done with deviations` → `🟡 In progress` and re-runs the three replacement slices through the fixed seam. Rejected: accepting 0/3 and continuing unchanged (P5.3/P5.4 consume the same description-free carrier shape, so P5.4's economic verdict would measure our carrier gap and spend five more one-shot rows on a foregone `NO-GO` before the `2026-08-12` expiry); the contract-level fix adding `task.scenario` (frozen `business-dispatch-admission-v1@1.0.0` refuses unknown fields, so it forces a 14-admission re-mint, a full P5.1 rewrite and a grant covering every remaining row, and buys nothing the hash-verified catalog resolution does not already deliver — recorded instead as a P6 product-surface follow-up); reopening only P5.5 and leaving P5.2 `🟠` (P5.4 would start with no positive business-edit precedent). **Consequences:** three items lose terminality at once and P5.1 stops being the phase's one cleanly terminal item; every downstream G2B pin moves again to the `generation_hash` recomputed at P5.5's second re-freeze; the v1 carrier set stays byte-frozen and the eleven unused D105 rows keep their existing bindings, so P5.3/P5.4 need no re-mint; `findings/P5-repository-pilot.md`'s execution record, safety and reversibility claims all remain valid — only its causal reading of the zero-diff records changes, and it changes against our own harness rather than against the provider. RAG:✅ 2026-08-06 two `perplexity-web` Deep Research passes over `claude-code-action`, OpenHands, SWE-agent, the SWE-bench harness, Crystal, Uzi, claude-squad, vibe-kanban, container-use and FleetCode establish that no surveyed harness dispatches a coding task as a file list without a natural-language description and that the documented outcome of an under-specified prompt is precisely a no-op/empty diff the agent labels success (`findings/P5.2-external-harness-precedent-2026-08-06.md`); owner-grounded: `brief/34-p5.2-zero-accept-owner-decision-2026-08-06.md`; repo-grounded: `findings/P5.2-task-description-gap-2026-08-06.md` F1–F7, `research/38-p5.2-zero-accept-root-cause-and-options.md`.

elements.name: why
elements.value: A pilot that never states the task measures the harness, not the candidate; fixing it at the one producer that already owns the seam, using a hash the admission itself pins, restores the measurement without touching a single frozen byte or invented authority.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: [OWNER-GRANT:G-OWNER-P5.2-RETRY] Asked what to do about the `claude-code` wall-clock budget if a fresh batch is granted, the owner literally selected «Поднять до 600000 ms в новых строках (реком.)», having already selected the option whose own text authorizes «новый `[OWNER-GRANT]` на три ЗАМЕНЯЮЩИЕ строки P5.2 (новые trial ID, append под новым грантом)» (`brief/34-p5.2-zero-accept-owner-decision-2026-08-06.md`, both answers quoted verbatim there). The grant authorizes exactly three replacement P5.2 repository-slice trials — new distinct trial IDs, one slice each, `reusable:false`, same three scenarios/file scopes/frozen base `bde07fb0` and same two providers as the spent v1 rows, with the `claude-code` row's `timeout_ms` raised from `180000` to `600000` and every other cap unchanged. They are minted by P5.1 into an ADDITIVE v2 carrier set (own catalog/request/grants/replay/admissions/index files, own `catalog_hash`) so that not one v1 byte and not one existing `task_hash` moves. Scope of the grant, exhaustively: three dispatches, one fresh process each, no retry of a started attempt, no fourth slice, no raw provider content, no change to provider pins, no D105 row consumption, no extension of D105's `2026-08-12T23:59:59Z` expiry or its 14-row count. The three spent v1 P5.2 rows stay spent and are not re-minted, reset or reused; they remain historical evidence of the null measurement. **Consequences:** P5.2's acceptance is now judged against the v2 rows, so `validate-repository-pilot.py` must pin the v2 admission index and the raised budget explicitly rather than inheriting v1 constants; the raised `600000` ms applies only to the new `claude-code` row and creates no precedent for P5.3/P5.4, whose rows keep `180000`; if the fixed prompt still produces a `WALL_TIMEOUT` at 600000 ms, that is a first-class provider fact rather than a confounded one (`findings/P5.2-task-description-gap-2026-08-06.md` F5). RAG:— (owner-grounded: `brief/34-p5.2-zero-accept-owner-decision-2026-08-06.md` Q1/Q2 literal answers; repo-grounded: spent v1 rows in `artifacts/P5/repository-pilot-results-v1.json`, D105 carrier set and `phases/P5.md` P5.1).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Only a fresh, separately identified batch can turn a null measurement into a real one, and raising exactly the one budget that produced an uninterpretable observation — while changing nothing else — keeps the retry a controlled experiment rather than a second variable-rich attempt.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: [OWNER-SELECTION:P5.4-ECONOMIC-ADJUDICATION] Shown two facts verified first-party this pass — (a) the candidate lane writes provider usage as BOOLEANS (`usage_observed`/`cost_observed` in `providers/{codex,claude_code}.py`), not one integer, so no `economy-evidence-v1` metric field is ever populated; (b) no single provider exports all seven `metric_fields`: claude-code does not report `reasoning_tokens` separately (they are definitionally inside `output_tokens`) and codex reports no cost at all, while price lookup/imputation is forbidden by D25 and P5.4's own Scope Excluded — the owner literally selected «single-provider claude-code + economy-evidence-v2 (реком.)» (`brief/35-p5.4-economic-adjudication-owner-decisions-2026-08-06.md` Q1). The terminal economic adjudication therefore runs in `provider_scope.mode = single-provider` on `claude-code`, which `economy-evidence-v1` itself permits only «with a non-empty prior Owner D# reference» — D123 is that reference — and P1's frozen contract set is unfrozen for exactly one additive successor, `root/contracts/economy-evidence-v2.md`, carrying exactly three rule changes and no new field, formula, threshold, verdict or relaxed floor: (1) provider-structural inclusion (a field the provider does not report separately because it is definitionally contained in another reported field is a MEASURED `0` with a mandatory `inclusion_basis`; instantiated exactly once, for claude-code `reasoning_tokens` ⊂ `output_tokens`), (2) structural coordinator zero (an envelope of a component that makes no model call is a measured all-zero envelope with a mandatory `zero_basis` file reference — Artifex's coordinator is deterministic by D3), (3) single-provider economic scope never reported as parity. D123 supersedes D14 ONLY in that its `GO` may now rest on a single-provider economic lane; every D14 threshold (`<25%`, `≥2×`, `N=5`, «unknown measurement запрещает GO») is unchanged, and D25's ban on imputing a missing metric stands — rules (1)/(2) are measured values with a named basis, not imputations. **Consequences:** `economy-evidence-v1` stops being the adjudication contract for P5.4 and P6 (it stays frozen and archived as the predecessor, unedited); P1's six-contract aggregate freeze is re-cut as an eight-contract v2 manifest; the plan can no longer claim provider parity from its economic verdict; and codex, having no cost surface that rule (1) can rescue, is structurally outside the economic lane. RAG:✅ 2026-08-06 provider usage-surface verification (`findings/P5.4-metric-surface-gap-2026-08-06.md` F10, `perplexity-web` + first-party `.claude/runs/*.json`); owner-grounded: `brief/35-…` Q1; repo-grounded: `findings/P5.4-metric-surface-gap-2026-08-06.md` F9, `root/contracts/economy-evidence-v1.md`.

elements.name: why
elements.value: A frozen field list that no available provider can fill makes `GO` unreachable by construction; the owner chose to fix the contract's unknown rules honestly on the one lane that can supply real integers, rather than to fabricate numbers or to quietly drop the economic claim the brief asks for.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: [OWNER-SELECTION:P5.4-BASELINE-LANE] Shown that no incumbent lane exists — all four `artifacts/P0/baseline-catalog.json` rows carry `eligible_for_battle_wave: false`, the only `eligible_for_matching` row is `classification: synthetic` with four null token fields, and P5.4 declares no producer, harness or `Files` entry for a live comparator — the owner literally selected «Прямой headless-вызов провайдера тем же скриптом (реком.)» (`brief/35-…` Q2). The `baseline` lane is henceforth defined as: the SAME slice, base commit, acceptance refs, validation set, provider, model class, effort and budget envelope as its paired candidate wave, executed as ONE headless single-shot provider invocation WITHOUT the supervisor, launched by a plan-local runner that itself performs no model call — so the baseline `coordinator` envelope is a structural zero under D123 rule (2) and the `worker` envelope is extracted by the SAME code path as the candidate's. The catalog's `baseline_lane` vocabulary `live-manual`/`live-harness-run`/`live-workflow` is retired for P5.4 rows and replaced by the single value `live-direct-provider`; `baseline_evidence_class: live-paired` is unchanged and is now satisfiable. D14 branch 2 (matched Workflow) is NOT pursued: the owner did not select it and no carrier exports a Workflow coordinator envelope per attempt, so it stays `BRANCH2_UNKNOWN` and disables only itself. **Consequences:** the measured claim narrows honestly to worker-vs-worker with a provable coordinator zero on both sides — this design can no longer claim a coordinator-context saving it does not measure (which D7 already forbade calling a saving); P0's baseline catalog is superseded as P5.4's comparator source without being edited (its rows stay exactly as frozen, and the `synthetic` row remains inadmissible); and the wave count doubles from five dispatches to ten. RAG:— (owner-grounded: `brief/35-…` Q2; repo-grounded: `artifacts/P0/baseline-catalog.json`, `root/contracts/economy-evidence-v1.md` lane/match rules, `research/39-p5.4-forward-topology.md` §2).

elements.name: why
elements.value: An incumbent lane that a human drives cannot export a coordinator envelope the executor can observe, so it could never satisfy the contract; making the incumbent a scripted headless call of the same provider on the same slice is the only comparator this repository can actually measure, and it is exactly the question the owner asked — supervisor versus doing it directly.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: [OWNER-GRANT:G-OWNER-P5.4-PAIRED-WAVES] branch=`p5-paired-battle-waves`; consumer=`P5.1 mints, P5.4 spends`; providers=`claude-code` only (`Claude Code 2.1.222`, honored through `SKM_CLAUDE_BIN` per D120); maximum_dispatch_count=`10` — five `candidate` rows and five `baseline` rows, one dispatch each, `max_slices:1`, `reusable:false`, no retry of a started attempt; trial_ids=`p5.4w-wave-0{1..5}-*` (candidate) and `p5.4b-wave-0{1..5}-*` (baseline), each baseline row copying its candidate twin's scenario, kind, `historical_patch_sha256`, files, `base_commit`, route, capabilities, `acceptance_refs`, `validation` and budgets VERBATIM and differing only in `trial_id`, `controlled_root`, `lane` and `order`; controlled_roots=`mktemp:p5-p5-4-<trial_id>` for all ten; per_trial_caps=`max_slices:1, timeout_ms:900000, max_envelope_bytes:65536, max_event_count:512, max_turns:40, max_output_bytes:65536, token_limit:200000, cost_limit_microunits:5000000`; expiry=`2026-09-30T23:59:59Z`; revoked=`false`; owner-message=`brief/35-p5.4-economic-adjudication-owner-decisions-2026-08-06.md` Q3. The owner literally selected «Поднять до max_turns 40 / timeout 900000 ms / token_limit 200000 (реком.)», whose option text also named `max_output_bytes` 16384→65536 and `max_event_count` 64→512; `max_slices`, `max_envelope_bytes` and `cost_limit_microunits` are byte-equal to D105 and were not raised. Two parameters are composed by this design pass from the selected option's own shape, exactly as D105 was composed from `brief/22` and D122 from `brief/34`, and are auditable against `brief/35-…`: the expiry `2026-09-30T23:59:59Z` (the remediation chain contains a frozen-contract freeze and two producer reopens, so binding this grant to D105's `2026-08-12` clock would guarantee forfeiture before the first dispatch) and the ten trial IDs/roots. Carriers are minted by P5.1 as an ADDITIVE v3 set with its own catalog/request/grants/replay/admissions/index and its own `catalog_hash`; not one v1 or v2 byte moves. **Consequences:** the five unused `p5.4-wave-*` D105 rows are written off explicitly — they are never re-minted, reset or reused, they keep `used_slices: 0`, and they will simply expire unspent on `2026-08-12T23:59:59Z` together with the other six unused D105 rows; D105's 14-row ceiling and expiry are NOT extended by this grant; and the raised caps apply only to these ten rows, creating no precedent for any other item. RAG:— (owner-grounded: `brief/35-…` Q3 literal answer; repo-grounded: D105/D122 carrier shape, `artifacts/P5/trial-catalog-v1.json` P5.4 rows, `findings/P5-repository-pilot.md` §8 measured turn exhaustion).
