elements.value: The frozen budgets were empirically disproven — a real editing dispatch exhausted 8 turns on three files and an earlier one hit the 180 000 ms wall — so dispatching ten irreversible one-shot grants under them would have measured the budget rather than the candidate; a single new grant of the same shape as D122 raises exactly the caps that bound and nothing else.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: [OWNER-SELECTION:P5.4-CLAUDE-ONLY-WAVES] Shown that the codex lane is blocked by its own bubblewrap sandbox, that the only verified path is `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (which forfeits the `network-disabled`/`SEC-WORKTREE` guarantee on a host with confirmed outbound network), and that the compensating control — an externally created network namespace — was tested first-party this pass and does not work on this kernel (`unshare -rn` → `Operation not permitted`, the same restriction that produces codex's own `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`), the owner literally selected «Все пять волн на claude-code, codex исключён из P5.4 (реком.)» (`brief/35-…` Q4). All ten D125 rows are `claude-code`; waves 01 and 04, previously codex, keep their scenarios, file scopes and historical patches and change provider only. D126 supersedes P5.4's Implementation Rules requirement «Terminal success requires both providers» and, correspondingly, the Scope Excluded entry «single-provider waiver into terminal readiness», BOTH only for the P5.4 adjudication: provider parity remains a live, separately carried acceptance obligation proven by terminal P3.3 (provider parity/exit conformance) and P5.3 (both-provider recovery/failure evidence), and P6 continues to consume that parity evidence from its actual carriers. `G-OWNER-P5.4-SINGLE`, retired by D85, is NOT revived — it was a verdict-only gate and authorized no dispatch; D126 authorizes dispatch scope, not a waiver of any floor. **Consequences:** P5.4 stops being the carrier of provider-parity evidence and its terminal packet must say so explicitly rather than implying parity; the codex business lane remains unproven for business dispatch and P6 may not claim it as a shipped capability without its own evidence; and the sandbox/network trade-off stays undecided and open rather than being resolved by silence. RAG:✅ 2026-08-06 first-party namespace probe and the recorded codex sandbox diagnosis (`findings/P5.4-metric-surface-gap-2026-08-06.md` F11, `findings/P5-repository-pilot.md` §8); owner-grounded: `brief/35-…` Q4.

elements.name: why
elements.value: Spending two irreplaceable one-shot grants on a lane whose blocker is an unresolved security trade-off would have bought refusals, not measurements, and dropping to N<5 would have predetermined `NO-GO` by wave count alone.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P5.4's forward path is decomposed into five items in execution order **P5.6 → P5.7 → P5.5 → P5.1 → P5.4** (`research/39-p5.4-forward-topology.md` §4), and the coupling surface is named up front. New item **P5.6** consolidates the generation-aware repair of the four frozen gates that are red on the current tree for one shared cause — `artifacts/P5/validate-shadow.py`, `artifacts/P3/validate-package-promotion.py`, `artifacts/P5/validate-repository-pilot.py` and the `124df816` P4 evidence anchor (F1/F2/F4/F5) — applying the pattern D121/D122 rule (6) already established for `validate-trial-admissions.py`. New item **P5.7** freezes `economy-evidence-v2` under D123 and re-cuts the aggregate contract manifest as an additive `contract-manifest-v2.json` enumerating all eight contracts, which also closes F3 (D108's own additive `business-dispatch-admission-v1.md` reads as directory drift to the frozen six-contract aggregate). **P5.5** reopens a third time as the sole producer of package bytes (D119) to export measured provider economy — the seven `economy-evidence-v2` metric fields as integers, with `inclusion_basis`/`zero_basis` where the rule applies — and to re-freeze both G2B manifests; its scope is inside D108's existing `exact scope` list (`providers/{codex,claude_code}.py`, `activity.py`, `cli.py` and their tests), so no new grant is created and, as D119 proved, the re-freeze runs with zero provider processes. **P5.1** reopens a third time as the sole carrier producer (D121) to mint the additive v3 set for D125's ten rows. Rejected: four separate reopens of P5.1/P3.8/P1.5/P4.7 for the gate repairs (reopening two closed phases to change plan-local validator scripts costs more bookkeeping than it buys, and P1.5's own reopen is required for D123 anyway, where it is scoped to the contract, not to the validators); and letting P5.4 repair its own gates or mint its own carriers (measurement self-certification, banned by D119/D121). **Coupling surface (files touched by ≥2 of these items):** `artifacts/P5/validate-repository-pilot.py` (P5.6 repairs it; P5.4 re-runs it as a gate), `artifacts/P1/validate-economy-evidence.py` and `contract-manifest-v2.json` (P5.7 authors, P5.4 consumes), `artifacts/P5/business-successor-{generation,assurance}-v1.json` (P5.5 re-freezes, P5.1 and P5.4 pin), `artifacts/P5/validate-trial-admissions.py` (P5.1 extends for v3, P5.4 runs), `phases/P5.md` (every item). **Consequences:** P5.5 and P5.1 lose their `🟠 Done with deviations` terminality for the third time and must re-earn it, phase P5 grows from five items to seven, and the plan's earliest possible `GO` moves behind a frozen-contract freeze — the cost of not having discovered F9/F10 at design time. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `research/39-p5.4-forward-topology.md`, `findings/P5.4-preflight-blockers-2026-08-06.md`, `findings/P5.4-metric-surface-gap-2026-08-06.md`, D108/D119/D121/D122).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Each blocker is fixed by the item that already owns the surface it lives on, so no item authors evidence about itself; consolidating the four same-cause gate repairs into one item avoids reopening two closed phases for mechanical work.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P5.6's escalated question is resolved with a THIRD option: `validate-shadow.py`'s `business carriers exist before exact owner grant` guard is a ONE-TIME HISTORICAL fact, so it MOVES rather than being relaxed or retired — in `validate()` it is asserted at the shadow-freeze commit resolved at run time (all four frozen carriers share exactly one commit, `17cf14cd`), through `git ls-tree`; in `main()` it becomes a refusal raised BEFORE `--write` writes its first byte, where «the freeze may not be re-cut once carriers exist» is true forever. Alternatives rejected: relax-in-place alone leaves `--write` able to overwrite the freeze and keeps the check running AFTER the write it should prevent; retiring the non-`--write` mode would trade four live green invariants (catalog/mapping/shadow/request drift, frozen G2 predecessor pin) for one stale line, and the analogy with the inert read-only `repository-pilot-results-v1.json` does not hold for an active re-derivation. `research/40-p5.6-gate-reconciliation-design.md` §1. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.6-gate-staleness-verification-2026-08-06.md` §1)

elements.value: Правило `findings/P5-retry-carrier-set.md` §3 («расширять item, только когда починка ровно одна») соблюдено, а не обойдено: после первичной проверки фактов остаётся ровно одна связная починка, и это не одна из двух, между которыми эскалация предлагала выбрать. Право принять это конструктивное решение без владельца — `brief/36-p5.6-constructive-authority-owner-direction-2026-08-06.md`

Two further defects in the same line are fixed with it: the item's `--prototype` literal was `artifacts/supervisor` while the script requires `artifacts/P3/adapter-manifest-v1.json` (so every run died on an argument check before reaching the gate), and passing `--historical-commit` ALONE would silence F2 rather than repair it — that branch skips the current-tree comparison entirely, so the live half (current package equals the sole G2B digest) must be added. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.6-gate-staleness-verification-2026-08-06.md` §2, `validate-package-promotion.py:79-104`)

elements.name: why
elements.value: Литерал в Validation ломал гейт до его сути; «якорь» переставал быть выбором, как только историю манифеста прочитали, а не пересказали

elements.name: decision
elements.value: `validate-repository-pilot.py` answers two different questions with one exit code, and P5.2's `0/3 accepted` is immutable recorded evidence (its three D122 admissions are one-shot and spent) — so the script can NEVER exit 0, and both P5.6's own «exits 0» and P5.4's pre-intent gate «`validate-repository-pilot.py` green» were unreachable as authored. The verdicts are split by exit code: `0` = evidence intact AND every slice accepted; `2` = evidence intact with the honest partial/zero-acceptance report; `1` = structural failure, staleness or mutated bytes. Consumers gate on «not `1`». P5.4's pre-intent gate sentence is re-worded accordingly in this design pass (P5.6 must not edit another item's acceptance). Alternatives rejected: grepping the output text makes a gate depend on a prose string (the class that greens on a blank); an owner exemption would place «expected red» inside the last gate before release — exactly the state P5.6 exists to end. `research/40-p5.6-gate-reconciliation-design.md` §3. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.6-gate-staleness-verification-2026-08-06.md` §3)

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P5.6's Implementation Rule (5) required every commit intervening on the P4 anchor «to touch only P4 evidence paths», which rejects the ONLY correct anchor `3533234c` — a legitimate P4.7 remediation (`fix(harness): восстановить committed-tree validation P4`) that repaired the P4 validators and the harness half of the same defect in one `Files`-scoped commit. The rule is reformulated: the P4-EVIDENCE PORTION of each intervening commit's diff must be owned by a P4 item or the P4 phase close; other paths in the same commit are recorded and do not stop the item, while a P4-evidence change no P4 item accounts for still does. The new anchor is corroborated twice independently: `git diff --exit-code 3533234c -- phases/P4.md artifacts/P4` is empty, and the frozen P5.1 `trial-catalog-v1.json` pins the same tree as its `source_tree_ref`. Boundary: `124df816` also names the owning snapshot of the historical P4.8 leaf validator (P5.1 Scope/Rules/Validation, D106) and those occurrences do NOT move. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.6-gate-staleness-verification-2026-08-06.md` §4–§5)

elements.name: why
elements.value: Правило смешивало «легитимна ли правка P4-улик» (существенный вопрос) с «трогал ли коммит что-то ещё» (к path-scoped `git diff` отношения не имеет) и гарантировало вторую эскалацию на собственном верном якоре

elements.name: decision
elements.value: P5.5 reopens a FOURTH time as the sole package producer (D119) to register the authority the owner already granted in D125: `business_dispatch.GRANT_BATCHES` gains a `D125` row (marker `[OWNER-GRANT:G-OWNER-P5.4-PAIRED-WAVES]`, `trial-admission-index-v3-p5.4-paired.json`, `trial-catalog-v3-p5.4-paired.json`, `expected_count` 10), and — the design decision `brief/37` §5 delegated to this pass — the `branch` literal MOVES INSIDE the batch row (`load_indexed:118` reads the selected batch's own `branch` instead of the hardcoded `p5-business-trials`), so batch identity has exactly one carrier. The alternative selected AGAINST is a data-driven batch table read from a plan-local manifest: it would move the authorized-batch set out of reviewed code into a file written by the same layer that mints the carriers (an authority-semantics change, i.e. an owner gate, not a designer's constructive decision under `brief/36`), and it would pay a contract-sized cost now for a benefit that arrives only at a NEXT grant — while D125 is by construction this plan's last grant (P6 dispatches nothing), which `root.speculative-work` forbids. The registration commit carries the seventh G2B re-freeze and its ledger entry, exactly as the D122 registration did (`6755be6b`, ledger `7a44f9bc…`). **Consequences:** D127's «third and by design final reopen» wording for P5.5 no longer holds — this is the fourth, and the claim was falsified by the same class it was written under; P5.5 loses `🟠` terminality again; the seventh G2B freeze invalidates any literal generation pin laid before it, which is why D133's gate repairs are ordered after it; and the two grant batches that today share one branch literal stop sharing it, so a branch swapped between D105 and D122 rows — undetectable until now — refuses. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.4-package-authority-gap-2026-08-06.md` §3–§4 and its two-change 10/10 proof, `findings/P5.4-forward-conformance-sweep-2026-08-06.md` §1, `research/41-p5.4-package-authority-remediation.md` §2, `packages/artifex/lib/artifex/business_dispatch.py:31-38,84,117-118`, `activity.py:148`; owner-grounded: D125, `brief/37` §5).

elements.name: why
elements.value: The owner granted the authority and P5.1 minted its carriers, but the seam that must spend them was never taught the grant — the missing work is producer-side registration, not a design question; and moving the branch into the row closes the second half of the same class instead of leaving it for the next grant to rediscover.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: New item **P5.8** consolidates the three gate defects that today are owned by NO live item, applying the settled two-sided pattern (D121/D122 rule 6, D130 ledger membership): (1) `artifacts/P5/validate-recovery-pilot.py` compares its recorded `g2b_generation_hash` with `!=` against the live manifest (line 124) and therefore can never go green after any re-freeze — repaired to ledger membership plus «ledger last entry equals live generation», with the `--ledger` argument the script does not yet have; (2) `artifacts/P4/validate-assurance.py` recomputes `g2.package_files` from the current tree and fails `G2 manifest drift` because the package legitimately advanced to G2B — repaired two-sided (frozen G2 side proven against its own snapshot, live side against the current G2B generation resolved at run time), keeping `--contracts contract-manifest-v1.json` because the P4 freeze is a six-contract fact and the v2 aggregate is P5.7's forward artifact; (3) the latent `TypeError` in `artifacts/P1/validate-economy-evidence.py:lane_units` — `duration_ms`/`turns` are summed without the `None` guard the token/cost fields have, while `economy-evidence-v2` explicitly admits a `null` metric with an `unknown_reasons` entry — repaired so an unknown propagates as unknown and blocks its branch, never as a silent `0` and never as a crash. Rejected: reopening P5.6 (its Scope Included is an exhaustive four-repair list already closed with its evidence; three more repairs is not the «exactly one repair» case `findings/P5-retry-carrier-set.md` §3 allows an item to be extended for) and reopening P5.3 (its six one-shot D105 trials are spent; returning terminal evidence to `🟡` to edit a validator buys nothing). Execution order is **P5.5 → P5.8 → P5.4**, derived not chosen: repair (1) survives only as ledger membership, and the ledger's last entry becomes the seventh freeze inside P5.5. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.4-forward-conformance-sweep-2026-08-06.md` §2–§3/§6 with each failing command and output, `findings/P5-paired-wave-carrier-set.md` §6, D127/D130/D131, `root/contracts/economy-evidence-v2.md` lines 119–125).

elements.name: why
elements.value: Four red gates everyone «knows are expected» is exactly the state P5.6 existed to end; leaving two of them unowned while P5.4's pre-intent gate names one of them would put a permanent exemption inside the last gate before release.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: The P4-evidence anchor stays `3533234c` and is NOT retargeted; D134 supersedes D131 ONLY in the anchor gate's machine form, adding one explicitly authorized exception class. P5.8's repair (2) edits `artifacts/P4/validate-assurance.py`, a P4-evidence path, so the gate becomes TWO commands: `git diff --exit-code 3533234c -- plans/2026.08.03-ARTIFEX-SUPERVISOR/phases/P4.md plans/2026.08.03-ARTIFEX-SUPERVISOR/artifacts/P4 ':(exclude)plans/2026.08.03-ARTIFEX-SUPERVISOR/artifacts/P4/validate-assurance.py'` (every other P4 byte still byte-identical) AND `git log --format=%h 3533234c..HEAD -- plans/2026.08.03-ARTIFEX-SUPERVISOR/artifacts/P4/validate-assurance.py` returning EXACTLY ONE commit, P5.8's item commit (the excluded path's whole intervening history is the authorized repair and nothing else). Retargeting the literal to P5.8's commit was rejected on a fact, not a preference: `3533234c` is corroborated by a second independent carrier — the `source_tree_ref` of the frozen `trial-catalog-v{1,2,3}` carriers pins that exact tree — and those carriers may never be re-pinned, so a retarget would destroy the anchor's own corroboration and leave a literal resting on itself. Named blind spot: the exclusion is blind to the CONTENT of `validate-assurance.py`, which is why the second command is mandatory — without it the exclusion would be a hole through which any P4-evidence change could pass. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.4-forward-conformance-sweep-2026-08-06.md` §3 with the literal's full consumer sweep, D131, `artifacts/P5/trial-catalog-v1.json` `source_tree_ref`). **Consequences:** the anchor gate stops being a single copy-pasteable command and every consumer of its sentence (P5.4's pre-intent gate, P5.5's and P5.8's Validation) must carry both halves — a gate that is cheaper to run than to read correctly is how the previous form got quoted with the wrong argument list twice.

elements.name: why
elements.value: D131 already ruled that the substantive question is whether a P4-evidence change is legitimately owned, not whether some commit touched something else; an authorized forward repair is exactly that case, and expressing it as an exclusion plus a provenance proof keeps the anchor's second corroboration intact.

elements.name: decision
elements.value: F15 is resolved INSIDE P5.4 and creates no package work: `run-battle-waves.py` imports `artifex.activity.BusinessProviderActivityPort` and reads the measured `economy` envelope off its return value for the candidate lane, and reaches the same extraction for the baseline lane through the public `claude_code.fold_business_records` with a request built by `business_dispatch.request` (D124's «the same measurement extraction», satisfied without re-implementing it). Exposing `economy` through `cli.py`'s `dispatch-business-intent` — P5.5's other named exit — is NOT done: it would write a package byte, hence force an EIGHTH G2B re-freeze, for a convenience the runner does not need. If a later item surfaces the field on the CLI anyway, the runner may simply read it there; nothing in this decision forecloses that. RAG:— (repo-grounded: `findings/P5.4-package-authority-gap-2026-08-06.md` §5, `findings/P5.5-measured-economy-envelope.md` §6, `packages/artifex/lib/artifex/cli.py:246-249`, `security.py:98-114`; owner-grounded: D119 reserves every package byte to P5.5).

elements.name: why
elements.value: The measured envelope already exists on the port's return value; adding a CLI field to read what the runner can import would buy one JSON key at the price of another irreversible generation freeze.
